rationale: This is a mechanical recombination of two already-archived signals (Recognized-Intangible Cash Insolvency and Recognized-Intangible Earnings Insolvency) using the exact MIN-of-two-insolvency-ranks template already tested in R&D Dual-Failure Fragility, and both archived parents already delivered stronger alpha (-0.053/-0.058) than the intersection is likely to add, so it is a near-duplicate rather than a new mechanism.

The construction is internally consistent and the diagnosis (positive slope but negative alpha implies the high-relief tail contains unproductive R&D) motivates a genuine conditioning change, though the MIN means the composite's long leg may be dominated by the (ib+xrd)/lt profitability leg, which is close to a known profitability/distress anomaly and should be benchmarked against that leg alone.

Expression, hypothesis and negative expected sign are mutually consistent (all legs coded so that high values mean high fragility, with a non-negative R&D weight preserving direction), and adding an operating-cash shortfall to the archived maturity-mismatch signal is a substantive rather than cosmetic refinement of a signal that had the right slope but no alpha.

This is the third variant of the same soft-collateral-versus-short-debt idea and differs from the archived Maturity Gap and Positive Funding Gap only in the scaling of the funding-balance leg (an arbitrary dlc+che+at denominator), so it reads as a cosmetic re-parameterization; note also that the archived RANK×RANK version already produced a large reliable alpha with a null Fama-MacBeth slope, and nothing here addresses that specific inconsistency.

Swapping the net-liability conditioner for loss severity is an economically motivated change of state variable rather than a re-parameterization, and the signed organic-minus-acquired contrast is coherent with the positive expected sign, though the archived parent's weak Fama-MacBeth slope (0.552) alongside a significant alpha warns that the payoff may again be concentrated in the extreme legs rather than monotone.

This is a direct splice of two archived signals — it reuses the exact loss-severity conditioner of the Pre-R&D Earnings Distress Separator and the exact adjusted-gross-surplus leg of R&D-Adjusted Gross-Surplus Coverage — and since both "earnings before R&D over liabilities" and "gross surplus after R&D over liabilities" proxy the same construct, the change amounts to a numerator substitution with high expected correlation to the archived result.
